facts.text: On this date in 1973, the Sydney Opera House opened — after a budget overrun of 1,457%. Original estimate: $7 million. Final cost: $102 million.
On this date in 1944, US forces returned to the Philippines. MacArthur had promised to return 2 years and 10 months earlier, and kept a recording ready to broadcast the moment he waded ashore.
Mongolia has a lower population density than any sovereign nation on Earth — roughly 2 people per square kilometer, less than the open ocean averages in maritime shipping lanes.
The Philippines has more islands than it has officially counted. The total revised from 7,107 to 7,641 after a 2016 satellite survey — meaning 534 islands simply went unrecorded for decades.

Toronto is the most ethnically diverse city on the planet by share of foreign-born residents, with over 50% of its population born outside Canada — a higher proportion than New York, London, or Dubai.

On this day in 1987, global markets were still reeling from Black Monday — the Dow had lost 22.6% in a single session two days prior, the largest single-day percentage crash in US history, dwarfing even 1929.
On this day in 1935, Mao's Long March ended — within decades, the nation those survivors built would become the world's largest holder of US Treasury debt.

The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree. The entire market capitalization of the companies traded that day would not cover a single hour of today's S&P 500 trading volume.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion valuation in 2019, making it worth more than the entire GDP of Italy — a country of 60 million people with 2,000 years of economic history.
The word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium' — the allowance Roman soldiers received to buy salt. The commodity once scarce enough to pay armies now costs less per pound than a postage stamp.

On this date in 1968, Tommie Smith and John Carlos were stripped of their Olympic credentials — but the biology of their raised fists endures: sustained defiance activates the same neural reward circuits as physical victory.
Your skeleton is not static. Every decade, your entire bone mass is silently replaced, atom by atom, through a process called remodeling — the femur you were born with no longer exists.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. One teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.

On October 20, 1947, the Hollywood blacklist began — but the human memory encoding those events uses the same hippocampal replay mechanism as rats navigating mazes, firing in compressed bursts during sleep.

Mantis shrimp see 16 types of color receptors compared to humans' 3, yet process color worse — their eyes transmit raw data directly to limbs for instant reaction, bypassing conscious perception entirely.

On this day in 1968, Jacqueline Kennedy married Aristotle Onassis — five years after Dallas, four months after Bobby's assassination. The world was scandalized. She was 39 and had outlived two Greek tragedies already.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain sent image signals over wire while Morse code was still considered cutting-edge.

On this day in 1818, the US and Britain agreed the 49th parallel would divide their claims west of the Great Lakes. Canada as a border was negotiated before most of its land had been walked by a single European.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC. The pyramid was finished around 2560 BC. Armstrong landed in 1969.
Nintendo was founded in 1889 — the same decade Nietzsche went mad, van Gogh cut off his ear, and the Eiffel Tower opened. It sold playing cards for 70 years before it touched a joystick.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh word for a longing toward a home you cannot return to — or one that never existed. Untranslatable, yet immediately understood.
On this day in 1968, Jacqueline Kennedy married Aristotle Onassis, prompting the Italian press to coin 'Jackie-O' — a nickname that stuck far longer than the marriage.
Mamihlapinatapai: a single Yaghan word for the look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Guinness record-holder for most succinct word.

On Oct. 20, 1973, the Sydney Opera House opened — and its sail-like shells have a word: 'synclastic surfaces,' curves that bend the same way in all directions, borrowed from mathematics into architecture.
On this date in 2021, Shiba Inu's market cap briefly surpassed Ford Motor Company — a token created as a joke in August 2020 outvalued a 118-year-old automaker with $136B in annual revenue.
On this date in 2017, CME Group announced Bitcoin futures, a decision that structurally changed BTC's price ceiling — regulated short-selling became possible for the first time.
Bitcoin's timechain has never produced an orphan block lasting more than one block deep in practice — the longest confirmed chainsplit resolved in under 2 minutes, in March 2013.
Ethereum's EIP-1559, live since August 2021, has permanently destroyed over 4.4 million ETH — the fee-burn mechanism turned transaction demand directly into deflationary pressure on supply.
Satoshi Nakamoto's known wallet addresses have remained untouched since May 2010 — any movement from those ~1.1 million BTC would be detectable within seconds by nodes worldwide.

On this date in 2022, DeepMind's AlphaCode placed in the top 54% of competitive programmers on Codeforces — the first AI to perform at that level on novel problems, not benchmarks designed around its training.
On this date in 2017, Google's paper 'Attention Is All You Need' appeared on arXiv, introducing the transformer — the architecture now underlying virtually every large language model in production.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have cost over $100 million in compute. The original GPT, trained in 2018, cost roughly $43,000. That's a 2,000x cost increase in five years.
RLHF — the technique that made ChatGPT behave like an assistant rather than a text predictor — was first described in a 2017 OpenAI paper about teaching robots to do backflips in simulation.

The Chinchilla paper (2022) showed that most large language models were undertrained relative to their size. The field had been scaling parameters while starving models of tokens — a foundational error at massive expense.
